Selection of a vendor for an enterprise resource planning replacement. A five-person procurement review panel at a logistics company evaluates the shortlisted vendors for replacing its enterprise resource planning system. One vendor will be contracted. Participants: Benjamin, Midori, May, Ryuji and Misaki. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.

- Board minutes on capital and operating requests
- Five years of renewal invoices
- Support ownership during last winter's outage
- Warehouse rule changes after new accounts
- Upgrade history of the dispatch tool
- Data lift in the 2018 pay move
- Depot calendar and the peak-season cutover
- Yard devices and the 2021 scheduling trial
- Administrator retirements and hiring times
- Depot supervisors and the last rollout

The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Midori, Ryuji, May, Misaki and Benjamin. |---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |

## Participants
Name: Benjamin
Age: 28
Gender: male
Personality: Benjamin is an intelligent and calm person. He is able to think calmly and rationally, and even in emotional situations, he places importance on logic. In public, he is elegant and polite, often incorporating sarcasm and humor into his conversations, but he is skilled at doing so without hurting others, creating a harmonious atmosphere. He also has an introverted side, often engrossed in deep thought, and occasionally keeps his distance from those around him. However, his calmness and knowledge are factors that earn him the trust of others even in difficult situations.
Concern: Money here gets approved in one shape and refused in another, and a headline price has stopped telling me what a system will really cost us over its life. What worries me is the part of the bill that keeps arriving after everyone has stopped watching.

Name: Midori
Age: 38
Gender: female
Personality: Midori has a calm and kind personality. She is friendly to everyone and listens to the concerns and problems of those around her, offering reliable advice. She can be a little shy, often acting reserved with people she meets for the first time, but once she opens up, she shows her bright and energetic side. She loves cooking and has a domestic side, but she also has a spirit of adventure and enjoys trying new things. She values balance in both her work and personal life and places importance on harmony with those around her.

Age: 24
Gender: female

Name: Ryuji
Age: 28
Gender: male
Personality: Ryuji has a calm and cautious personality, and is the type of person who always assesses the situation before acting. He rarely shows his emotions, and spends his time thinking deeply about many things. His friends consider him to be serious and reliable, but his expressionless attitude can sometimes make them feel uneasy. He tends to judge things based on reason rather than intuition, and strongly sticks to his beliefs. He is very independent and often does things at his own pace.
Concern: The part that keeps me awake is the depot floor: freight moves whether or not the office is mid-project, and the equipment out there is nobody's idea of modern. Anything we bring in has to survive our calendar and our yards as they actually are.

Name: Misaki
Age: 24
Gender: female
Personality: Misaki has a calm personality and tends to deal with things in a cool-headed manner. She may seem a little unfriendly at times, but she is actually very kind at heart and does not hesitate to lend a helping hand to those in need. She does not express her emotions outwardly and does not talk much about her relationships with those around her, but she is often relied upon by those close to her. - A: Meridian Systems. A vendor offering a hosted suite covering finance, inventory, and transport planning, delivered through a fixed configuration process and supported by a regional service team.
- B: Tessera Cloud Suite. A vendor offering a subscription platform with configurable workflows and an application marketplace, with a partner firm handling data migration and staff training.
- C: Corvus Platform. A vendor providing a modular system assembled from separate finance, warehouse, and fleet components, each licensed and configured independently of the others.
- D: Anchor Industrial Software. A vendor supplying a system built specifically for transport operators, deployed on the company's own servers with an engineering team present through rollout.

Cards (see the schedule above; title: text):
- Board minutes on capital and operating requests: Capital requests have been trimmed three years running in the board minutes, while recurring operating lines passed the same meetings with barely a question.
- Five years of renewal invoices: Finance lined up five years of renewal invoices: bundled agreements held their price, separately licensed pieces and add-ons climbed yearly, and the company's one outright purchase cost only maintenance.
- Support ownership during last winter's outage: The current contracts scatter support across four suppliers, and last winter's outage sat unowned for two days while each of them pointed at another.
- Warehouse rule changes after new accounts: Two new distribution accounts arrived mid-year and forced the warehouse rules to be rewritten twice; the scope frozen at project start never survived a full year.

- Data lift in the 2018 pay move: When driver pay moved to a new system in 2018, an external team did the data lift; mismatched route codes kept surfacing for a year afterwards.
- Depot calendar and the peak-season cutover: Depots run around the clock from November through January with no freeze window; the one cutover attempted in that stretch cost two days of paper dispatch.
- Yard devices and the 2021 scheduling trial: Yard scanners and driver handhelds are a mix of older models, and the general scheduling tool trialled in 2021 was ringed with spreadsheets within a month.
- Administrator retirements and hiring times: Two of the four administrators who know the company's systems from the inside retire this year, and the last posting for those skills stayed open eleven months.
- Depot supervisors and the last rollout: Depot supervisors have shaped their own routines over years; standard steps taught by visiting trainers in the last rollout were quietly dropped in two depots within weeks.
